units.text: Aspose.Cells FOSS for Java reads and writes Excel files in the .xlsx format. It converts workbooks by loading existing files and saving modified versions, supporting operations such as cell value assignment, style formatting, row height and column width adjustment, and document property updates. It also handles workbook loading diagnostics, including repair attempts and issue reporting for malformed files. Conditional formatting and data validation rules can be applied to worksheet ranges and saved to output files.

It manages workbooks and worksheets through the Workbook class, which owns a WorksheetCollection of Worksheet objects, allowing add, remove, rename, and visibility control per sheet, while each worksheet exposes a Cells collection for reading and writing string, numeric, boolean, date/time, and formula values.

It applies full cell styling and formatting through the Style class, which carries font, borders, fill, alignment, number format, and protection flags, set via Cell.getStyle() and setStyle(), with NumberFormat supporting built-in Excel number-format codes.

It enforces data validation and conditional formatting on worksheet ranges via ValidationCollection and ConditionalFormattingCollection, both scoped to CellArea, supporting validation types like whole numbers with operators and conditional formatting based on cell values.

It provides load diagnostics and repair through LoadOptions with strict-mode toggles and package/XML repair flags, and Workbook.getLoadDiagnostics() returns a report with repair details and preservation notes for unsupported package parts encountered during load and save.

It supports embedded content such as cell comments with author, text, visibility, and size via CommentCollection, and images from bytes, streams, or file paths with two-cell anchor positioning via PictureCollection, which detects JPEG, PNG, GIF, and BMP formats.

It renders charts and shapes by creating 18 of the 25 ChartType values programmatically via ChartCollection.add(), while the remaining 7 ChartEx types round-trip verbatim from loaded workbooks, and ShapeCollection adds, retrieves, and removes 38 preset AutoShapeType geometries.
Create a new workbook, set up a worksheet named Report with formatted data in cells A1 and B1, adjust row height and column width, and save the result as report.xlsx.
Load a potentially corrupted Excel file with repair options enabled, print any diagnostic messages, update the document author property, and save the repaired workbook as output.xlsx.

Aspose.Cells FOSS for Java reads and writes Excel workbooks in the .xlsx format, supporting workbook creation, data manipulation, and formula storage for round-trip preservation.

Saving is currently limited to .xlsx, and ChartEx types (Waterfall, Treemap, Sunburst, Histogram, Box and Whisker, Funnel, and Map) cannot be created programmatically; charts of these types loaded from an existing workbook are preserved verbatim across load and save.

Formulas are stored and round-tripped, but the library is not a full spreadsheet calculation engine, and a handful of public XML-mapper classes are unimplemented skeleton code carried over from an early scaffold.
Some APIs exist mainly to preserve OOXML metadata and package fidelity rather than to provide full Excel feature parity.

The project requires JDK 17 or later and Maven as the build tool. It depends on Apache POI only in test scope and never at runtime. The test suite is located under src/test/java/org/aspose/cells_foss/ and includes scenario-driven integration tests for workbook behavior and XLSX round-tripping, as well as fast, focused unit tests for individual API classes without XLSX I/O.
It adds additional spreadsheet save formats beyond .xlsx, a full formula calculation engine, ChartEx chart type creation, and dedicated enterprise support.
